chunks: 3 - He said: Abul Hasan Ali ibn Khalid al-Maraghi reported to me, he said: Ali ibn Sulaiman narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Nahawandi narrated to us, he said: Abu al-Khazraj al-Asadi narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn al-Fudhayl narrated to us, he said: Aban ibn Abu Ayyash narrated to us, he said: Ja'far ibn Iyas narrated to us, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said:

He said: Once a slain person was found during the time of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family, so he went out, peace be upon him, deeply enraged until he ascended the pulpit. He praised Allah and extolled Him, then said:

"A man from among the Muslims is killed and no one knows who killed him?! By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if all the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth gathered together to kill a believer or were pleased with it, Allah would surely cast them all into the Fire."
"And by the One in Whose Hand is my soul, no one flogs another unjustly except that he will be flogged the same way tomorrow in the fire of Hellfire."
"And by the One in Whose Hand is my soul, no one harbors hatred toward us, the Ahlul Bayt, except that Allah will throw him on his face into the fire of Hellfire."

key_terms.أهل البيت: The People of the House; the Prophet's household, specifically his family members
key_terms.المنبر: The pulpit; the raised platform from which the Prophet delivered sermons in the mosque
key_terms.قتيل: A slain person; one who has been murdered
key_terms.مؤمن: A believer; one who has faith in God and Islam
key_terms.والذي نفسي بيده: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul; a solemn oath formula used by the Prophet

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about killing a believer and hating the Ahlul Bayt?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) delivered an impassioned sermon after the body of a murdered Muslim was discovered in Medina, the identity of whose killer was unknown. Ascending the pulpit in visible anger, he made three solemn oaths invoking God: first, that all inhabitants of heaven and earth who participate in or approve of killing a believer will be cast into Hell; second, that anyone who unjustly flogs another will receive the same punishment in Hellfire; and third, that whoever harbors hatred toward the Ahlul Bayt will be thrown face-first into Hellfire. This hadith links the inviolability of Muslim life with love for the Prophet's household, themes central to early Islamic community ethics.
